# Agent hooks: deterministic code at fixed points of a turn

<!-- practices:learn:start (generated by scripts/practices/practices.py; do not edit) -->
**Learn this:** [Agent hooks](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/practices/explainers/claude-hooks/index.html) (explainer with a [quiz](https://github.com/evocaslab/hq/blob/main/practices/explainers/claude-hooks/index.html#quiz)). Learner path: Working with agents, step 5.
<!-- practices:learn:end -->

A **hook** is a program the agent tool runs at a named point of its loop: before a tool call, after it, when the turn
ends, when a session starts. `CLAUDE.md` is advice the model may weigh and forget; a hook is enforcement the model cannot
talk its way past. Use advice for taste and hooks for rules that must hold. This page covers Claude Code (read
2026-11-08 from its docs, see Sources); other tools are in [Portability](#portability). The guard side of it is in
[guards.md](guards.md#hook-semantics-claude-code), the pull-loop `Stop` hook in
[autonomous-sessions.md](autonomous-sessions.md#stop-hook-for-the-pull-loop).

## The model: event, matcher, handler, answer

- **Event.** The point of the loop. Per session: `SessionStart` (matcher `startup`, `resume`, `clear`, `compact`),
  `SessionEnd`. Per turn: `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`. Per tool call: `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse`,
  `PostToolUseFailure`. Around helpers and memory: `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`. Also
  `Notification`, `FileChanged`, `CwdChanged`, `WorktreeCreate`, `ConfigChange` and more; the list grows, read the reference.
- **Matcher.** Narrows an event: a tool name (MCP tools are `mcp__<server>__<tool>`), a list `Edit|Write`, or a
  regex. Events without a matcher (`UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`) ignore it silently.
- **Handler.** `command` (a program; the default and the reliable one; `args` gives an exec form with no shell
  quoting), `http`, `mcp_tool`, `prompt` (one cheap model call that answers ok or not) and `agent` (experimental
  sub-agent). An optional `if` (permission-rule syntax) filters tool events further; `timeout` is in seconds.
- **Input.** The program gets JSON on stdin: `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `hook_event_name`, `permission_mode`,
  and per event `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_response`, `prompt`, `last_assistant_message`, `stop_hook_active`.
- **Answer.** Exit 0 and optional JSON on stdout; exit 2 and a reason on stderr; any other code is a non-blocking error
  shown to the user (unless the handler sets `onFailure: "block"`).

| Answer | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| exit 0, plain stdout | context for the model on `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`; elsewhere ignored (on `PreCompact` it steers the summary) |
| exit 0, JSON `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` `allow\|deny\|ask` (+ reason) | `PreToolUse` verdict; the strictest of several hooks wins; a hook cannot loosen a permission rule, and a `deny` holds even in bypass mode |
| exit 0, JSON `updatedInput` / `additionalContext` | rewrite the tool input; add up to 10,000 characters of context |
| exit 2, stderr | **blocks** on `PreToolUse`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `SubagentStop`, `PreCompact`; only informs on `PostToolUse`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`; ignored by `PermissionRequest` |
| JSON `decision: "block"` + `reason` | the same block for `Stop`, `SubagentStop`, `PostToolUse`, `UserPromptSubmit` |
| JSON `continue: false` | stops the agent outright, beating every other field |

## Scopes, async, caps

- **Scopes** merge, none replaces another: user `~/.claude/settings.json`, project `.claude/settings.json`,
  `.claude/settings.local.json`, managed policy, plugin `hooks/hooks.json`, and the frontmatter of a skill or subagent
  (active while it runs). The same hook in two scopes **runs twice**: register once, at the widest scope that needs it.
  Admins can switch hooks off or allow only managed ones.
- **Parallel and ordered.** Hooks on one event run in parallel; do not depend on order or on seeing each other's edits.
- **Async.** `async: true` runs in the background and cannot block; its context arrives on the next turn. `asyncRewake:
  true` keeps the timeout and, on exit 2, wakes an idle session with the output as a system reminder (the wake-up of a
  waiting session). Both are killed when a one-shot (`-p`) run ends. Check the desktop app separately: parity with the
  terminal is not documented.
- **Caps.** A `Stop`/`SubagentStop` block may repeat 8 times with no tool call between; a tool call resets it. So a
  `Stop` hook is a nudge, not a gate. Default timeouts: 600 s command, 30 s `prompt`, 60 s `agent`, but 30 s on
  `UserPromptSubmit`, and `SessionEnd` shares a budget of about 1.5 s unless you raise `timeout`.
- **Environment.** `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` for paths (never a relative path: the hook's cwd moves), `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`
  (on `SessionStart` and a few others) to export variables to later shell calls.

## Which event for which job

| Job | Event | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Refuse a dangerous or unwanted call | `PreToolUse` | exit 2 with what to do instead; fail closed |
| Rewrite or annotate a call | `PreToolUse` | `updatedInput`, `additionalContext` |
| Answer a permission prompt by policy | `PermissionRequest` | JSON `decision.behavior`; exit 2 does not apply |
| Format or lint what was written | `PostToolUse` on `Edit\|Write` | idempotent tools only; findings come back as context |
| Inject facts at the start | `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit` | keep it short; it costs context every time |
| Keep working until a check passes | `Stop` | cap 8; test `stop_hook_active`; the real gate stays elsewhere |
| Verify a helper's hand-back | `SubagentStop` | the agent type is often just `general-purpose`: read the role from the brief's `Role:` line at the head of `agent_transcript_path`; internal helpers fire the event too |
| Steer what survives compaction | `PreCompact` | stdout becomes summary instructions |
| Record or clean up | `SessionEnd` | tiny file write; start slow work detached |
| Tell a person | `Notification` | async; dedupe repeats |

## Rules

1. **A hook enforces, an instruction advises.** If a miss costs real damage or a repeat, make it a hook; keep the
   advice in the instructions file too, so the model knows why it was stopped.
2. **Fast and cheap.** Every call pays the hook's time. Aim for tens of milliseconds on `PreToolUse`; do the slow part
   async, detached, or not at all. No network call on a hot path.
3. **Fail safe, on purpose.** Decide per hook what a crash or a timeout means. A security guard fails closed
   (`onFailure: "block"`); a convenience hook fails open and must never hang the turn.
4. **Exit 2 blocks; the message is the instruction.** Say what to do instead, in one or two lines. Exit 1 does not block.
5. **No secrets** in hook files, `--debug` logs or the context you inject; read them from the environment of the process.
6. **Idempotent and re-entrant.** The same event may fire again (resume, retry, a second scope); a block must not
   re-block forever (`stop_hook_active`, a counter in a file).
7. **Test with piped stdin.** `echo '{"hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"..."}}' |
   ./hook; echo $?` for each allow, deny and malformed case, in a unit test that lives with the hook. Also test the
   empty input and a huge input.
8. **A hook that claims state needs a release.** A hook that takes a claim, lease or lock (the next backlog item, a
   marker file) must release it on every exit path, including the cap and a crash, and probing it by hand needs the
   same release; otherwise the probe strands work.
9. **Log and count.** One line per block or ask to a file, so a repeating prompt becomes a fix ([guards.md](guards.md)).
10. **One registration.** Check `/hooks` or the merged settings for doubles after editing any scope.

## Portability

The core (`SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`, stdin JSON, exit 2 to
block) is shared by several tools; the details differ. Facts from each tool's docs (read 2026-11-08):

| Tool | Where | Compatibility with the Claude Code format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex CLI | `hooks.json` or `[hooks]` in `config.toml`, trusted in `/hooks` | high: same names, stdin JSON, `permissionDecision` (no `ask`), exit 2; `command` and `mcp_tool` handlers only |
| Copilot CLI | `.github/hooks/*.json`; also reads `.claude/settings.json` | high: PascalCase event names switch to Claude's payloads; timeouts fail open |
| Junie CLI | `hooks` in the user `config.json` only | medium-high: same stdin fields and `decision`; short default timeouts |
| Gemini CLI | `hooks` in `settings.json` | medium: same shape, other event names (`BeforeTool`, `AfterAgent`) |
| Cursor | `hooks.json`, `version: 1` | partial: exit 2 works, own output fields (`permission`, `followup_message`) |
| Cline | SDK plugin functions | low: code API, not a settings file |
| OpenCode | TypeScript plugins, block by throwing | none: code, not JSON |
| Aider | no hooks; `--lint-cmd`, `--test-cmd` after each edit | none |

Claude-only: `ask`, `prompt` and `agent` handlers, `asyncRewake`, `Notification` matchers, `PreCompact` stdout as
instructions. To keep one policy across tools, write scripts that read the snake_case stdin and answer with
`hookSpecificOutput`, and treat each other tool's registration as a thin generated file.

## Ideas not adopted yet

Candidates, not rules; each needs a measure before and after.

- `PermissionRequest` answering proven-safe asks by the same proof the guard uses, so fewer prompts reach a person.
- `SubagentStop` check that a hand-back names a commit, a branch and the gate line, else block with the missing field.
- `SessionEnd` ledger check, so the retire check runs even when a session dies.
- `PreCompact` stdout listing what must survive (claims, branch, open requests) instead of saving a second copy.
- `Notification` to a phone or desktop for permission and idle prompts.
- `PostToolUse` async formatter on `Edit|Write`; a `prompt`-type `Stop` reviewer for workers (judgment: false blocks).
- Hooks in skill frontmatter, so a mode's hooks live only while it runs.
